_provenance.statement: Every file here was written by Snapmaker Orca 2.3.6 itself. A candidate key was placed on the object in an otherwise byte-identical project, Orca was started on it by an automation harness that owned its own process and never force-killed anything, and Orca was driven through Save Project As. What Orca wrote is what is stored. One variable per file. Nothing was hand-edited afterwards except the absolute source_file path, replaced with 'probe.3mf' so that no private path is tracked.
_provenance.geometry: a 30 mm cube - synthetic, no private model
_provenance.why_the_invented_key_matters: A key that survives while nonsense also survives has proved nothing. The invented key is dropped, so the three that survive are recognised rather than copied.
_provenance.the_sharpest_row: orca-dropped-unrecognised-key.3mf and orca-control-no-settings.3mf are BYTE-IDENTICAL. A project carrying an invented key, or PrusaSlicer fill_density, or PrusaSlicer support_material, comes back from Orca as the same file as a project that carried nothing at all. Copying the source key across is indistinguishable from writing nonsense.

orca-authored-three-overrides.3mf.note: Snapmaker Orca 2.3.6's own account of a per-object override. The three settings were set through Orca's own Process > Objects panel on a plain cube and Orca was asked to Save Project As. It wrote layer_height=0.3, sparse_infill_density=45% and enable_support=1 as <metadata> inside <object> in model_settings.config. That is the target vocabulary and the target structural level, stated by the target.

orca-control-no-settings.3mf.note: The control: the same project with nothing set, round-tripped. One object, no per-object metadata. This is what 'the object survived' looks like.

orca-dropped-unrecognised-key.3mf.note: What Orca writes back when the object carries a key it does not act on: nothing. Three different inputs produce this one file byte for byte - an invented key, PrusaSlicer's fill_density and PrusaSlicer's support_material. See input_sha256_all_producing_this_file.

orca-deleted-object-on-malformed-value.3.note: layer_height="not-a-number" on the object. Orca opened the project with an EMPTY PLATE: no object, no build item, no geometry file. A malformed per-object value does not fail safely - it takes the object with it.
